=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`_direct_inflight_review_run_on_branch` PR-named block; the `STALL_INFLIGHT_DIRECT_CHECK … outcome=pr_named_review_run` log line | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the PR-named fallback finds a match, the log line reuses `_di_runs_total` and `_di_runs_live` from the earlier branch-listing jq pipeline. Those counts describe the branch listing's runs, not the PR-named lookup, so the line conflates two unrelated metrics.
  WHY: This is purely a log-accuracy defect — control flow is fine — but it undermines post-incident triage of the very class of duplicate-dispatch / zombie-run bugs the fix is meant to make diagnosable.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`_has_active_autofix_run` head-branch loop versus PR-named fallback | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The head-branch loop iterates `queued in_progress` only, but the new PR-named jq filter accepts `pending` as well. A `pending` review run on the head branch (a duplicate dispatch held back by `cancel-in-progress: false`, per `agents.md`) would therefore slip past the head-branch check and then be caught only by the PR-named helper — which queries `workflow_dispatch` runs, so a `pending` `pull_request` run on the head branch would not be seen there either.
  WHY: A `pending` head-branch run does not suppress a new `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` call in `_has_active_autofix_run`, so the poller could dispatch a second review run while one is wedged in `pending` on the same head, re-introducing the duplicate-dispatch churn #4618/#4701 explicitly set out to prevent.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Issue #4926's plan ("Recognize consumer `ai-review.yml` PR-named dispatch runs in the §26 checker") — `_is_pr_dispatched_review_run` and `_active_run_count` should each accept the (`.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`, `AI Review [pr:{number}]`) pair alongside the `internal-review.yml` pair, so consumer repos do not lose hand-off recognition and active-run counting when they run the new default-branch dispatches.
  Expected change site: `.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py` (and twin `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py`) at `DISPATCHED_REVIEW_*` constants, `_is_pr_dispatched_review_run`, and `_active_run_count`.
  Evidence of absence: The PR's diff adds `DISPATCHED_REVIEW_WORKFLOW = ".github/workflows/internal-review.yml"` and a hard-coded `DISPATCHED_REVIEW_RUNS_PATH = "repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/internal-review.yml/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&per_page=100"`. `_is_pr_dispatched_review_run` still requires `path.split("@", 1)[0] == DISPATCHED_REVIEW_WORKFLOW`, and `_active_run_count` only matches `display_title == DISPATCHED_REVIEW_TITLE.format(number=pr_number)`. In a consumer repo, the active `ai-review.yml` dispatch run fails the path/title test and falls back to the 404-on-internal-review branch (which `test_dispatch_listing_404_counts_zero_and_other_errors_raise` pins as zero) — so a live consumer dispatch returns the same "no active run" verdict as no dispatch at all. The plan/log are committed (`docs/plans/issue-4926-consumer-review-handoff-plan.md`, `docs/implement-plan/issue-4926-consumer-review-handoff.md`) and show the phase as `BLOCKED — phase 1/1 protected-path approval`, with no in-PR implementation hunk for the consumer pair.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py / workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:`_active_run_count` `except ReadError as exc: if "HTTP 404" in str(exc):`
  Issue: Loose substring match on the `gh` error message; any future error string that contains "HTTP 404" as a substring would also be swallowed as zero.
  Suggested minimal fix: Switch to a structured `ReadError` field (e.g. check `exc.status == 404` if `gh_api` records it) or compare against the exact `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` prefix the current `gh` builds. Either way the matching is exact, not substring-based.
  Estimated lines changed: 3
